name: ISO/IEC 27001
summary: The certifiable standard for an Information Security Management System. It sets out governance, risk assessment and treatment, and a set of Annex A controls, with a cycle of continual improvement.
applies: Organisations wanting independently certifiable security assurance.

name: ISO/IEC 27002
summary: A detailed code of practice that explains how to implement the information security controls referenced by ISO 27001 Annex A. It is guidance, not a certifiable standard in its own right.
applies: Teams implementing or maturing their 27001 controls.

name: ISO/IEC 27005
summary: Guidance for information security risk management that supports the risk requirements of ISO 27001, covering how to identify, analyse, evaluate and treat risk.
applies: Building a defensible, repeatable risk method.

name: ISO/IEC 27017
summary: Cloud specific security guidance extending ISO 27002, with controls for both cloud service providers and the customers who use them.
applies: Organisations moving workloads to the cloud.

name: ISO/IEC 27018
summary: Controls for protecting personally identifiable information in public clouds where the provider acts as a processor of that data.
applies: SaaS and cloud providers handling customer PII.

name: ISO/IEC 27701
summary: A privacy extension to ISO 27001 and 27002 for a Privacy Information Management System, supporting obligations such as the GDPR and local privacy law.
applies: Demonstrating privacy governance to customers and regulators.

name: ISO/IEC 27035
summary: Guidance for planning, detecting, assessing, responding to and learning from information security incidents.

name: ISO 22301
summary: A management system for business continuity: preparing for, responding to and recovering from disruptive incidents so critical functions keep running.

name: ISO 31000
summary: Principles and guidelines for managing risk across the whole organisation, often used as the foundation that security risk work aligns to.
applies: Aligning security risk with enterprise risk.

name: ISO/IEC 42001
summary: The first management system standard for governing artificial intelligence responsibly, covering AI risk, transparency and lifecycle management.

name: NIST CSF 2.0
summary: Organises cyber risk management into six functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover. A common language that works for both the board and the technical team.
applies: A flexible, outcomes based security program.

name: NIST SP 800-53
summary: A comprehensive catalogue of security and privacy controls for information systems, used well beyond its US federal origins.

name: NIST SP 800-171
summary: Requirements for protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in non federal systems, commonly required through defence supply chains.

name: NIST SP 800-207
summary: The reference architecture for Zero Trust: verify explicitly, grant least privilege, and assume breach across every access decision.

name: NIST RMF (800-37)
summary: A lifecycle to categorise, select, implement, assess, authorise and continuously monitor the controls on a system.

name: CIS Controls v8
summary: Eighteen prioritised controls and safeguards grouped into Implementation Groups and mapped to other frameworks, giving a practical order of operations.

name: CIS Benchmarks
summary: Consensus configuration baselines for securely hardening operating systems, cloud services and common software.

name: MITRE ATT&CK
summary: A living knowledge base of real world adversary tactics and techniques, used for detection engineering, threat hunting and red and blue team exercises.

name: PCI DSS 4.0
summary: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard, mandatory for any organisation that stores, processes or transmits cardholder data.

name: SOC 2
summary: An AICPA reporting framework that attests to an organisation's controls over security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy.
applies: SaaS vendors proving control to customers.

name: CSA CCM
summary: The Cloud Security Alliance Cloud Controls Matrix, a cloud specific control framework and assessment tool mapped to major standards.

name: COBIT
summary: ISACA's framework for the governance and management of enterprise IT, linking business goals to IT and security controls.
applies: Aligning IT and security with governance.

name: OWASP ASVS & Top 10
summary: Application security verification standards and the widely used Top 10 web risks, underpinning secure development and application testing.

name: ASD Essential Eight
summary: Eight prioritised mitigation strategies with a Maturity Model scored from Level 0 to Level 3. Widely treated as the baseline expectation for Australian organisations.

name: ASD Mitigation Strategies
summary: The broader Australian Signals Directorate list of strategies to mitigate cyber security incidents, from which the Essential Eight is drawn as the top subset.

name: ACSC Information Security Manual
summary: The Australian Cyber Security Centre's risk based cyber security framework and control set for protecting systems and data.

name: Protective Security Policy Framework
summary: Australian Government protective security policy spanning security governance, information, personnel and physical security.

name: Australian Privacy Principles
summary: Thirteen principles under the Privacy Act 1988 that govern how personal information is collected, used, disclosed and secured.

name: Notifiable Data Breaches
summary: Mandatory obligations under the Privacy Act to notify affected individuals and the regulator when an eligible data breach occurs.

name: Security of Critical Infrastructure Act
summary: Obligations for critical infrastructure entities, including risk management programs, incident reporting and enhanced security expectations.

name: APRA CPS 234
summary: A prudential standard requiring APRA regulated entities to maintain information security capability proportionate to the threats they face.

name: IRAP
summary: The Information Security Registered Assessors Program: independent assessment of systems and cloud services against the ISM.

name: Right Fit For Risk
summary: A security accreditation for employment services providers, built on ISO 27001 and the Essential Eight.
applies: Providers to the employment services sector.

name: Defence Industry Security Program
summary: A membership program that sets security requirements for businesses working with the Department of Defence.

name: NZ Information Security Manual
summary: New Zealand's baseline cyber security controls for government systems, published by the GCSB.

name: Protective Security Requirements
summary: New Zealand's protective security policy across governance, information, personnel and physical security.
applies: NZ public sector and its suppliers.

name: NZ Privacy Act 2020
summary: New Zealand's privacy law and Information Privacy Principles, governing personal information and including breach notification.
